current_episode.title: Doggie dream come true is business success story for Caz Burness

guest.bio_context: Kaz Burness spent 23 years in various roles at TK Maxx, the fashion retailer, including security, customer service, and stock room work. In February 2019, she began offering pet sitting and dog boarding services from her home, which grew during the COVID-19 pandemic where she supported key workers. She left TK Maxx in January 2022 to run her pet business full-time, and in October 2022, acquired Beacon Barkers kennels with her husband Darren, using a £100,000 loan from BCRS Business Loans.

pending_qa.q: How did a home-based pet care business transition to acquiring a commercial kennels facility?
pending_qa.r: Kaz started with doggy daycare and home boarding from her house in February 2019, then added dog walking in 2021. She worked at TK Maxx while building the business for about a year and a half before leaving in January 2022. When a kennels opportunity came up for sale in October 2022, she and her husband Darren acquired it, realizing it was the expansion she had been dreaming of but hadn't known how to achieve.

pending_qa.q: What factors influenced the choice of a finance provider for a business acquisition?
pending_qa.r: Kaz initially approached several finance companies but felt let down by their attitude toward lending, their plans, and unhelpful paperwork. When introduced to BCRS Business Loans, she found they believed in the business dream and understood the goals from the first conversation. A BCRS representative visited the house, reviewed the five-year plan, and was blown away by their vision, helping to expedite the paperwork to meet the October deadline for the kennels acquisition.

pending_qa.q: How can alternative finance companies support business growth beyond providing capital?
pending_qa.r: BCRS not only provided the £100,000 loan but also demonstrated genuine belief in the business vision. They sent a representative to the house to understand the five-year plan, and that person prioritized getting the paperwork through quickly—even while on holiday—to help meet the critical October half-term deadline when the business needed financial income to invest in repairs and operations.

pending_qa.q: What youth training and volunteer opportunities can a kennels business create?
pending_qa.r: Beacon Barkers actively encourages volunteering and work experience opportunities. They had one volunteer, a girl in her first year of veterinary nurse training, attending two days per week. In June, three year-10 work experience girls trained as kennel hands for a week. They are also hosting a vet student from Liverpool University volunteering during university holidays, and plan to explore apprenticeships next year to train people from start to becoming full head kennel personnel.

pending_qa.q: How has acquiring a business impacted employment and staff retention?
pending_qa.r: Since taking over the kennels in October 2022, Beacon Barkers has taken on an additional full-time groomer, a second full-time dog walker named Rachel, and has not lost a single member of staff. Kaz attributes this success to working with staff, listening to them, offering upskilling opportunities, improving staff benefits, and demonstrating ownership commitment by getting involved in day-to-day work like cleaning kennels, creating a team environment where everyone is pulling together.

pending_qa.q: What are the key lessons for business owners planning to acquire a business or access finance?
pending_qa.r: Kaz emphasizes that Rome wasn't built in a day and that entrepreneurs must have and stick to a five-year plan while remaining flexible. She stresses the importance of letting your head rule your heart, managing people well, understanding finances, and forecasting costs and subscription schedules. She also advises exploring finance options beyond traditional banks, noting that companies like BCRS exist as alternatives, and recommends shopping around to find the right fit—if a finance company doesn't feel right, change to someone else.

pending_qa.q: What are the expansion plans for a growing pet care business?
pending_qa.r: Beacon Barkers plans to launch doggy daycare by the end of April (originally planned for month two of the five-year plan but shifted to month eight to ensure proper sequencing). They aim to grow the grooming business under new groomer Kayleigh's vision. For year two, Kaz plans to open a secure dog walking field where dogs can be off-lead, rent sections to agility trainers, and potentially offer training facilities to police dog trainers.
